newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka 1996 trade deficit lower at $1.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka 1996 trade deficit lower at $1.3 bln.

text.p: Sri Lanka's 1996 trade deficit dropped to $1.28 billion or 9.4 percent of GDP from $.1.36 or 11.6 percent of GDP in the previous year, the Central Bank said in its annual report released on Wednesday.
Sri Lanka's exports grew by 13 percent in 1996 to SDR 2.85 billion, compared to a 12 percent rise the previous year, the report said.
Imports rose by seven percent to SDR 3.73 billion, as against five percent the previous year, resulting in a lowering of the deficit, the report said.

The 13 percent rise in exports reflected increases in all major categories of exports, despite a setback suffered to agricultural and industrial activities due to a drought and resulting power cuts, it said.

Industrial exports recorded a growth of 10 percent to SDR 2.0 billion, agricultural exports grew by 21 percent to SDR 662 million and export of mineral products rose by 15 percent to SDR 66 million, the report said.

All major categories of imports reflected significant increases, with consumer goods rising faster (nine precent growth) than other categories due to increse outlay on rice and wheat, the report added.
